prompt: Which address does every request to create, change or delete an Azure resource reach, whichever tool sent it?
hint: Lesson 1 read it from `az cloud show`.

choices.text: `login.microsoftonline.com`
choices.why: That is where the token comes from, the step before.

choices.text: `management.azure.com`
choices.why: Right. Azure Resource Manager.

choices.text: `portal.azure.com`
choices.why: The portal is one client; it too calls Resource Manager.

choices.text: `core.windows.net`
choices.why: That ends a storage account's data plane address.

prompt: Put the four steps of a request in order.
hint: The token comes before anything reaches Resource Manager.
items: the client gets a token from Microsoft Entra ID
the client sends the request to Resource Manager with the token
Resource Manager checks the token, role, policies, locks and limits
Resource Manager hands the request to the resource provider
trap: The provider does the work last, and only after every check passed.

prompt: The lab asked Entra ID for a token and got `AADSTS90002`. What does that code mean?
hint: Read the first sentence the lesson kept.

choices.text: The client secret was wrong
choices.why: Entra ID never got as far as the secret; it stopped at the tenant.

choices.text: The scope `management.azure.com/.default` is not allowed
choices.why: That is the usual scope for Resource Manager.

choices.text: The machine is not allowed to reach Entra ID
choices.why: Entra ID answered; the refusal is its own.

choices.text: The tenant in the address does not exist
choices.why: Right. `Tenant ... not found`.

prompt: In the filtered `--debug` output of `az group list`, what did the CLI do before it stopped?
hint: Read the three lines in order.

choices.text: It sent a GET to Resource Manager and was refused with 401
choices.why: No request was sent; the stop came before the token.

choices.text: It asked Entra ID for a token and was refused
choices.why: With no sign-in stored, there was nobody to ask a token for.

choices.text: Built a client for Resource Manager, then found no sign-in
choices.why: Right. `ResourceManagementClient`, then `Please run 'az login'`.

choices.text: It failed to find the `group list` command
choices.why: `Command table: group list` is the line where it found it.

prompt: A team argues that deploying with Terraform rather than the portal will get round an Azure Policy that denies public IP addresses. What does the lesson say?
hint: Where is a policy judged?

choices.text: It fails just as it would from the portal
choices.why: Right. Resource Manager judges every client's request; steps 2 to 4 are shared by every door.

choices.text: It works if the plan is approved first
choices.why: An approval in Terraform means nothing to Resource Manager.

choices.text: It works, because Terraform calls the providers directly
choices.why: No client calls a provider directly; Resource Manager stands in front of them all.

choices.text: It fails, because Terraform cannot create public IP addresses
choices.why: It can; the refusal is the policy's, not Terraform's.

prompt: A client asks Entra ID for a token for Resource Manager with the scope `https://management.azure.com/.___`.
hint: The word for what applies when nothing else is chosen.

prompt: Which HTTP method creates a resource, or replaces it with the body sent?
hint: It is idempotent.

choices.text: `POST`
choices.why: Resource Manager uses `POST` for actions such as restarting, not for creating resources.

choices.text: `PATCH`
choices.why: `PATCH` changes only the fields sent, such as tags.

choices.text: `GET`
choices.why: `GET` reads and changes nothing.

choices.text: `PUT`
choices.why: Right. Sending it twice leaves the resource as sending it once.

prompt: Why is `PUT` being idempotent the property lesson 26 builds on?
hint: What happens if a file is applied twice?

choices.text: It lets a deployment skip the permission checks
choices.why: Every `PUT` is checked like any other request.

choices.text: It makes each deployment faster than the one before
choices.why: Idempotence is about the result, not the time.

choices.text: Applying a file twice gives the same result
choices.why: Right. That is what lets Bicep and Terraform describe a whole environment.

choices.text: It deletes whatever the body does not mention
choices.why: That is complete mode, a different thing, in lesson 26.

prompt: `request.py` printed a full `PUT` for the network but not for the subnet. Why?
hint: Look at the subnet's `name` in the template.

choices.text: Its name is an expression
choices.why: Right. `[format(...)]`, which the program refused to guess.

choices.text: The subnet has no `location`, so it has no body
choices.why: A child resource takes its parent's place; its body still has `properties`.

choices.text: Subnets cannot be created through the REST API
choices.why: They can; a subnet is a child resource with its own URL.

choices.text: Bicep forgot to compile it
choices.why: It is in the template, with a `dependsOn` naming the network.

prompt: A pipeline sends the subnet's `PUT` before the network's, in parallel to save time. What does the lesson predict?
hint: What is a child resource without its parent?

choices.text: Both succeed, since Resource Manager queues them
choices.why: Ordering by `dependsOn` happens inside a deployment, not between separate requests.

choices.text: The subnet is refused, as its parent is missing
choices.why: Right. That order is what `dependsOn` gives a deployment.

choices.text: The network is created with the subnet already inside
choices.why: Two separate requests do not merge.

choices.text: The subnet is created in a default network
choices.why: There is no default network in Azure to fall into.

prompt: A file names `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks@2099-01-01`. What did `az bicep build` do?
hint: Was it an error or a warning?

choices.text: Warned, and compiled anyway
choices.why: Right. Whether the version exists is Resource Manager's question.

choices.text: Replaced it with the latest version it knew
choices.why: The template keeps the version written.

choices.text: Refused to compile, with an error
choices.why: It compiled; `BCP081` is a warning.

choices.text: Asked Resource Manager whether that version exists
choices.why: Building sends nothing anywhere.

prompt: Match each HTTP method to what it does in Resource Manager.
hint: One changes only the fields sent.

pairs.right: reads a resource or lists a collection
creates or replaces with the body sent

prompt: A request to create a VPN gateway is answered at once with 201 and an `Azure-AsyncOperation` header. What should the client do?
hint: When is the operation finished?

choices.text: Report success: 201 means the gateway exists
choices.why: 201 here starts a long operation; the state is not final yet.

choices.text: Send the same `PUT` again every second until it returns 200
choices.why: That spends write tokens and polls the wrong thing.

choices.text: Poll that address after `Retry-After` seconds
choices.why: Right. Until the state reads `Succeeded`, `Failed` or `Canceled`.

choices.text: Ask Entra ID for a new token
choices.why: The token is not the issue; the operation is still running.

prompt: The date after the `@` in a Bicep resource type becomes the URL's `api-___` parameter.
hint: It names a version.

prompt: A deployment fails with `MissingSubscriptionRegistration`. What is missing?
hint: Something has to be registered in the subscription.

choices.text: A role assignment for the deploying identity
choices.why: A missing role is `AuthorizationFailed`, a different error.

choices.text: The subscription's link to a management group
choices.why: A subscription may sit under the root and deploy normally.

choices.text: A budget for the subscription
choices.why: Budgets never block a deployment.

choices.text: The provider's registration
choices.why: Right. `az provider register --namespace ...` fixes it.

prompt: Why does Microsoft's documentation advise registering only the resource providers you use?
hint: Think of a stolen credential.

choices.text: Each registered provider is billed monthly
choices.why: Registration costs nothing; resources do.

choices.text: An intruder cannot use one never registered
choices.why: Right, and registration can add Microsoft applications to the tenant.

choices.text: Unregistered providers get faster updates
choices.why: Registration has nothing to do with updates.

choices.text: A subscription may register at most ten providers
choices.why: There is no such limit in the lesson.

prompt: A script has just emptied the subscription's read bucket. By Microsoft's figures, how many reads can it make in the next 4 seconds without being throttled?
hint: The refill is 25 a second.

prompt: A request is answered with 429 and `Retry-After: 6`. What does the lesson say a script should do?
hint: What happens to a request sent too early?

choices.text: Retry at once, since 429 is a temporary error
choices.why: A request before the time is refused again, and spends another token.

choices.text: Sign in again, since the token expired
choices.why: An expired token gives 401, not 429.

choices.text: Switch to another subscription to keep going
choices.why: That spreads a mistake, it does not fix it.

choices.text: Wait six seconds before the next request
choices.why: Right, and read the rate-limit headers to slow down before it happens.

prompt: Which of these are data plane operations? Choose all that apply.
hint: Using a resource, not managing it.

choices.text: Reading a blob at `shopassets.blob.core.windows.net`
choices.why: Right. The storage service answers, not Resource Manager.

choices.text: Changing a storage account's replication
choices.why: That configures the resource: control plane.

choices.text: Signing in to a virtual machine over SSH
choices.why: Right. Using the machine, not managing it.

choices.text: Reading a secret from `kv-shop-prod.vault.azure.net`
choices.why: Right. The vault itself answers.

choices.text: Creating a key vault
choices.why: Creating goes through `management.azure.com`.

prompt: Lesson 19 closes `shopassets.blob.core.windows.net` to the internet with a private endpoint. From a laptop outside the network, can ana still change the account's replication?
hint: Which plane do network rules close, and which plane is replication?

choices.text: Yes, through `management.azure.com`
choices.why: Right. Network rules apply to the data plane; managing still goes through Resource Manager.

choices.text: No, the private endpoint closes every address of the account
choices.why: It closes the data plane address, not Resource Manager.

choices.text: Only from Cloud Shell, which is inside Azure
choices.why: The control plane does not care where the client sits.

choices.text: Only after she reads a blob to prove access
choices.why: Data plane access does not grant control plane rights, nor the reverse.

prompt: In `PUT https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/bbbbcccc-1111-dddd-2222-eeee3333ffff/resourceGroups/rg-shop-prod/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/vnet-shop-prod?api-version=2024-05-01`, which piece says which properties the body may carry?
hint: It is a date.

choices.text: `Microsoft.Network`
choices.why: That names the provider who handles the request.

choices.text: `api-version=2024-05-01`
choices.why: Right. The version is the contract for the body.

choices.text: `rg-shop-prod`
choices.why: That is where the resource goes.

choices.text: `PUT`
choices.why: The method says what to do, not what the body contains.

prompt: Past the request limit, Resource Manager answers with HTTP status ___.
hint: Too Many Requests.
